1: # Welcome to DYNAMAX!
2: 
3: ![Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/probml/dynamax/main/logo/logo.gif)
4: 
5: ![Test Status](https://github.com/probml/dynamax/actions/workflows/run_tests.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)
6: ![Docstrings](https://github.com/probml/dynamax/actions/workflows/interrogate.yml/badge.svg)
7: [![DOI](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.07069/status.svg)](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07069)
8: 
9: Dynamax is a library for probabilistic state space models (SSMs) written
10: in [JAX](https://github.com/google/jax). It has code for inference
11: (state estimation) and learning (parameter estimation) in a variety of
12: SSMs, including:
13: 
14: -   Hidden Markov Models (HMMs)
15: -   Linear Gaussian State Space Models (aka Linear Dynamical Systems)
16: -   Nonlinear Gaussian State Space Models
17: -   Generalized Gaussian State Space Models (with non-Gaussian emission
18:     models)
19: 
20: The library consists of a set of core, functionally pure, low-level
21: inference algorithms, as well as a set of model classes which provide a
22: more user-friendly, object-oriented interface. It is compatible with
23: other libraries in the JAX ecosystem, such as
24: [optax](https://github.com/deepmind/optax) (used for estimating
25: parameters using stochastic gradient descent), and
26: [Blackjax](https://github.com/blackjax-devs/blackjax) (used for
27: computing the parameter posterior using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) or
28: sequential Monte Carlo (SMC)).
29: 
30: ## Documentation
31: 
32: For a highlevel summary, see [this JOSS 2024 article](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.07069).
33: 
34: For tutorials and API documentation, see: https://probml.github.io/dynamax/.
35: 
36: For an extension of dynamax that supports structural time series models, 
37: see https://github.com/probml/sts-jax.
38: 
39: For an illustration of how to use dynamax inside of [bayeux](https://jax-ml.github.io/bayeux/) to perform Bayesian inference
40: for the parameters of an SSM, see https://jax-ml.github.io/bayeux/examples/dynamax_and_bayeux/.
41: 
42: ## Installation and Testing
43: 
44: To install the latest releast of dynamax from PyPi:
45: 
46: ``` {.console}
47: pip install dynamax                 # Install dynamax and core dependencies, or
48: pip install dynamax[notebooks]      # Install with demo notebook dependencies
49: ```
50: 
51: To install the latest development branch:
52: 
53: ``` {.console}
54: pip install git+https://github.com/probml/dynamax.git
55: ```
56: 
57: Finally, if you\'re a developer, you can install dynamax along with the
58: test and documentation dependencies with:
59:

525:     r"""Abstract base class of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs).
526: 
527:     The model is defined as follows
528: 
529:     $$z_1 \mid u_1 \sim \mathrm{Cat}(\pi_0(u_1, \\theta_{\mathsf{init}}))$$
530:     $$z_t \mid z_{t-1}, u_t, \\theta \sim \mathrm{Cat}(\pi(z_{t-1}, u_t, \\theta_{\mathsf{trans}}))$$
531:     $$y_t | z_t, u_t, \\theta \sim p(y_t \mid z_t, u_t, \\theta_{\mathsf{emis}})$$
532: 
533:     where $z_t \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ is a *discrete* latent state.
534:     There are parameters for the initial distribution, the transition distribution,
535:     and the emission distribution:
536: 
537:     $$\\theta = (\\theta_{\mathsf{init}}, \\theta_{\mathsf{trans}}, \\theta_{\mathsf{emis}})$$
538: 
539:     For "standard" models, we will assume the initial distribution is fixed and the transitions
540:     follow a simple transition matrix,
541: 
542:     $$z_1 \mid u_1 \sim \mathrm{Cat}(\pi_0)$$
543:     $$z_t \mid z_{t-1}=k \sim \mathrm{Cat}(\pi_{z_k})$$
544: 
545:     where $\\theta_{\mathsf{init}} = \pi_0$ and $\\theta_{\mathsf{trans}} = \{\pi_k\}_{k=1}^K$.
546: 
547:     The parameters are stored in a :class:`HMMParameterSet` object.
548: 
549:     We have implemented many subclasses of `HMM` for various emission distributions.
550: 
551:     :param num_states: number of discrete states
552:     :param initial_component: object encapsulating the initial distribution
553:     :param transition_component: object encapsulating the transition distribution
554:     :param emission_component: object encapsulating the emission distribution
555: 
556:     """
557:     def __init__(self,
558:                  num_states : int,
559:                  initial_component : HMMInitialState,
560:                  transition_component : HMMTransitions,
561:                  emission_component : HMMEmissions):
562:         self.num_states = num_states
563:         self.initial_component = initial_component
564:         self.transition_component = transition_component
565:         self.emission_component = emission_component
566: 
567:     # Implement the SSM abstract methods by passing on to the components
568:     @property
569:     def emission_shape(self):
570:         """Return the shape of the emission distribution."""
571:         return self.emission_component.emission_shape
572: 
573:     def initial_distribution(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
574:                              inputs:Optional[Array] = None) \
575:                              -> tfd.Distribution:
576:         """Return the initial distribution."""
577:         return self.initial_component.distribution(params.initial, inputs=inputs)
578: 
579:     def transition_distribution(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
580:                                 state: IntScalar, 
581:                                 inputs:Optional[Array] = None) \
582:                                 -> tfd.Distribution:
583:         """Return the transition distribution."""
584:         return self.transition_component.distribution(params.transitions, state, inputs=inputs)
585: 
586:     def emission_distribution(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
587:                               state: IntScalar, 
588:                               inputs:Optional[Array] = None) \
589:                               -> tfd.Distribution:
590:         """Return the emission distribution."""
591:         return self.emission_component.distribution(params.emissions, state, inputs=inputs)
592: 
593:     def log_prior(self, params: HMMParameterSet) -> Scalar:
594:         """Compute the log prior probability of the model parameters."""
595:         lp = self.initial_component.log_prior(params.initial)
596:         lp += self.transition_component.log_prior(params.transitions)
597:         lp += self.emission_component.log_prior(params.emissions)
598:         return lp
599: 
600:     # The inference functions all need the same arguments
601:     def _inference_args(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
602:                         emissions: Array, 
603:                         inputs: Optional[Array]) -> Tuple:
604:         """Return the arguments needed for inference."""
605:         return (self.initial_component._compute_initial_probs(params.initial, inputs),
606:                 self.transition_component._compute_transition_matrices(params.transitions, inputs),
607:                 self.emission_component._compute_conditional_logliks(params.emissions, emissions, inputs))
608: 
609:     # Convenience wrappers for the inference code
610:     def marginal_log_prob(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
611:                           emissions: Array, 
612:                           inputs: Optional[Array]=None) -> float:
613:         """Compute the marginal log probability of the emissions."""
614:         post = hmm_filter(*self._inference_args(params, emissions, inputs))
615:         return post.marginal_loglik
616: 
617:     def most_likely_states(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
618:                            emissions: Array, 
619:                            inputs: Optional[Array]=None) \
620:                            -> Float[Array, "num_timesteps"]:
621:         """Compute the most likely sequence of states."""
622:         return hmm_posterior_mode(*self._inference_args(params, emissions, inputs))
623: 
624:     def filter(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
625:                emissions: Array, 
626:                inputs: Optional[Array]=None) \
627:                -> HMMPosteriorFiltered:
628:         """Compute the filtering distributions."""
629:         return hmm_filter(*self._inference_args(params, emissions, inputs))
630: 
631:     def smoother(self, params: HMMParameterSet, 
632:                  emissions: Array, 
633:                  inputs: Optional[Array]=None) \
634:                  -> HMMPosterior:
635:         """Compute the posterior smoothing distributions."""
636:         return hmm_smoother(*self._inference_args(params, emissions, inputs))
637: 
638:     # Expectation-maximization (EM) code
639:     def e_step(
640:             self,
641:             params: HMMParameterSet,
642:             emissions: Array,
643:            inputs: Optional[Float[Array, "num_timesteps input_dim"]]=None
644:            ) -> Tuple[PyTree, Scalar]:
645:         """The E-step computes expected sufficient statistics under the
646:         posterior. In the generic case, we simply return the posterior itself.
647:         """
648:         args = self._inference_args(params, emissions, inputs)
649:         posterior = hmm_two_filter_smoother(*args)
650: 
651:         initial_stats = self.initial_component.collect_suff_stats(params.initial, posterior, inputs)
652:         transition_stats = self.transition_component.collect_suff_stats(params.transitions, posterior, inputs)
653:         emission_stats = self.emission_component.collect_suff_stats(params.emissions, posterior, emissions, inputs)
654:         return (initial_stats, transition_stats, emission_stats), posterior.marginal_loglik
655:

15: def get_trans_mat(
16:         transition_matrix: Optional[Union[Float[Array, "num_states num_states"],
17:                                           Float[Array, "num_timesteps_minus_1 num_states num_states"]]],
18:         transition_fn: Optional[Callable[[IntScalar], Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]]],
19:         t: IntScalar
20: ) -> Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]:
21:     """
22:     Helper function to get the transition matrix at time `t`.
23:     """
24:     if transition_fn is not None:
25:         return transition_fn(t)
26:     elif transition_matrix is not None:
27:         if transition_matrix.ndim == 3: # (T-1,K,K)
28:             return transition_matrix[t]
29:         else:
30:             return transition_matrix
31:     else:
32:         raise ValueError("Either `transition_matrix` or `transition_fn` must be specified.")

34: class HMMPosteriorFiltered(NamedTuple):
35:     r"""Simple wrapper for properties of an HMM filtering posterior.
36: 
37:     :param marginal_loglik: $p(y_{1:T} \mid \theta) = \log \sum_{z_{1:T}} p(y_{1:T}, z_{1:T} \mid \theta)$.
38:     :param filtered_probs: $p(z_t \mid y_{1:t}, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots,T$
39:     :param predicted_probs: $p(z_t \mid y_{1:t-1}, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots,T$
40: 
41:     """
42:     marginal_loglik: Scalar
43:     filtered_probs: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"]
44:     predicted_probs: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"]
45: 
46: class HMMPosterior(NamedTuple):
47:     r"""Simple wrapper for properties of an HMM posterior distribution.
48: 
49:     Transition probabilities may be either 2D or 3D depending on whether the
50:     transition matrix is fixed or time-varying.
51: 
52:     :param marginal_loglik: $p(y_{1:T} \mid \theta) = \log \sum_{z_{1:T}} p(y_{1:T}, z_{1:T} \mid \theta)$.
53:     :param filtered_probs: $p(z_t \mid y_{1:t}, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots,T$
54:     :param predicted_probs: $p(z_t \mid y_{1:t-1}, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots,T$
55:     :param smoothed_probs: $p(z_t \mid y_{1:T}, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots,T$
56:     :param initial_probs: $p(z_1 \mid y_{1:T}, \theta)$ (also present in `smoothed_probs` but here for convenience)
57:     :param trans_probs: $p(z_t, z_{t+1} \mid y_{1:T}, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots,T-1$. (If the transition matrix is fixed, these probabilities may be summed over $t$. See note above.)
58:     """
59:     marginal_loglik: Scalar
60:     filtered_probs: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"]
61:     predicted_probs: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"]
62:     smoothed_probs: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"]
63:     initial_probs: Float[Array, " num_states"]
64:     trans_probs: Optional[Union[Float[Array, "num_states num_states"],
65:                                 Float[Array, "num_timesteps_minus_1 num_states num_states"]]] = None
66: 
67: 
68: def _normalize(u: Array, axis=0, eps=1e-15):
69:     """Normalizes the values within the axis in a way that they sum up to 1.
70: 
71:     Args:
72:         u: Input array to normalize.
73:         axis: Axis over which to normalize.
74:         eps: Minimum value threshold for numerical stability.
75: 
76:     Returns:
77:         Tuple of the normalized values, and the normalizing denominator.
78:     """
79:     u = jnp.where(u == 0, 0, jnp.where(u < eps, eps, u))
80:     c = u.sum(axis=axis)
81:     c = jnp.where(c == 0, 1, c)
82:     return u / c, c
83: 
84: 
85: # Helper functions for the two key filtering steps
86: def _condition_on(probs, ll):
87:     """Condition on new emissions, given in the form of log likelihoods
88:     for each discrete state, while avoiding numerical underflow.
89: 
90:     Args:
91:         probs(k): prior for state k
92:         ll(k): log likelihood for state k
93: 
94:     Returns:
95:         probs(k): posterior for state k
96:     """
97:     ll_max = ll.max()
98:     new_probs = probs * jnp.exp(ll - ll_max)
99:     new_probs, norm = _normalize(new_probs)
100:     log_norm = jnp.log(norm) + ll_max
101:     return new_probs, log_norm
102:

114: def hmm_filter(
115:     initial_distribution: Float[Array, " num_states"],
116:     transition_matrix: Optional[Union[Float[Array, "num_states num_states"],
117:                                       Float[Array, "num_timesteps_minus_1 num_states num_states"]]],
118:     log_likelihoods: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"],
119:     transition_fn: Optional[Callable[[IntScalar], Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]]] = None
120: ) -> HMMPosteriorFiltered:
121:     r"""Forwards filtering
122: 
123:     Transition matrix may be either 2D (if transition probabilities are fixed) or 3D
124:     if the transition probabilities vary over time. Alternatively, the transition
125:     matrix may be specified via `transition_fn`, which takes in a time index $t$ and
126:     returns a transition matrix.
127: 
128:     Args:
129:         initial_distribution: $p(z_1 \mid u_1, \theta)$
130:         transition_matrix: $p(z_{t+1} \mid z_t, u_t, \theta)$
131:         log_likelihoods: $p(y_t \mid z_t, u_t, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots, T$.
132:         transition_fn: function that takes in an integer time index and returns a $K \times K$ transition matrix.
133: 
134:     Returns:
135:         filtered posterior distribution
136: 
137:     """
138:     num_timesteps, num_states = log_likelihoods.shape
139: 
140:     def _step(carry, t):
141:         """Filtering step."""
142:         log_normalizer, predicted_probs = carry
143: 
144:         A = get_trans_mat(transition_matrix, transition_fn, t)
145:         ll = log_likelihoods[t]
146: 
147:         filtered_probs, log_norm = _condition_on(predicted_probs, ll)
148:         log_normalizer += log_norm
149:         predicted_probs_next = _predict(filtered_probs, A)
150: 
151:         return (log_normalizer, predicted_probs_next), (filtered_probs, predicted_probs)
152: 
153:     carry = (0.0, initial_distribution)
154:     (log_normalizer, _), (filtered_probs, predicted_probs) = lax.scan(_step, carry, jnp.arange(num_timesteps))
155: 
156:     post = HMMPosteriorFiltered(marginal_loglik=log_normalizer,
157:                                 filtered_probs=filtered_probs,
158:                                 predicted_probs=predicted_probs)
159:     return post
160:

263: def hmm_smoother(
264:     initial_distribution: Float[Array, " num_states"],
265:     transition_matrix: Optional[Union[Float[Array, "num_states num_states"],
266:                                       Float[Array, "num_timesteps_minus_1 num_states num_states"]]],
267:     log_likelihoods: Float[Array, "num_timesteps num_states"],
268:     transition_fn: Optional[Callable[[IntScalar], Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]]]= None,
269:     compute_trans_probs: bool = True
270: ) -> HMMPosterior:
271:     r"""Computed the smoothed state probabilities using a general
272:     Bayesian smoother.
273: 
274:     Transition matrix may be either 2D (if transition probabilities are fixed) or 3D
275:     if the transition probabilities vary over time. Alternatively, the transition
276:     matrix may be specified via `transition_fn`, which takes in a time index $t$ and
277:     returns a transition matrix.
278: 
279:     *Note: This is the discrete SSM analog of the RTS smoother for linear Gaussian SSMs.*
280: 
281:     Args:
282:         initial_distribution: $p(z_1 \mid u_1, \theta)$
283:         transition_matrix: $p(z_{t+1} \mid z_t, u_t, \theta)$
284:         log_likelihoods: $p(y_t \mid z_t, u_t, \theta)$ for $t=1,\ldots, T$.
285:         transition_fn: function that takes in an integer time index and returns a $K \times K$ transition matrix.
286: 
287:     Returns:
288:         posterior distribution
289: 
290:     """
291:     num_timesteps = log_likelihoods.shape[0]
292: 
293:     # Run the HMM filter
294:     post = hmm_filter(initial_distribution, transition_matrix, log_likelihoods, transition_fn)
295:     ll = post.marginal_loglik
296:     filtered_probs, predicted_probs = post.filtered_probs, post.predicted_probs
297: 
298:     # Run the smoother backward in time
299:     def _step(carry, args):
300:         """Smoother step."""
301:         # Unpack the inputs
302:         smoothed_probs_next = carry
303:         t, filtered_probs, predicted_probs_next = args
304: 
305:         A = get_trans_mat(transition_matrix, transition_fn, t)
306: 
307:         # Fold in the next state (Eq. 8.2 of Saarka, 2013)
308:         # If hard 0. in predicted_probs_next, set relative_probs_next as 0. to avoid NaN values
309:         relative_probs_next = jnp.where(jnp.isclose(predicted_probs_next, 0.0), 0.0,
310:                                         smoothed_probs_next / predicted_probs_next)
311:         smoothed_probs = filtered_probs * (A @ relative_probs_next)
312:         smoothed_probs /= smoothed_probs.sum()
313: 
314:         return smoothed_probs, smoothed_probs
315: 
316:     # Run the HMM smoother
317:     _, smoothed_probs = lax.scan(
318:         _step,
319:         filtered_probs[-1],
320:         (jnp.arange(num_timesteps - 1), filtered_probs[:-1], predicted_probs[1:]),
321:         reverse=True,
322:     )
323: 
324:     # Concatenate the arrays and return
325:     smoothed_probs = jnp.vstack([smoothed_probs, filtered_probs[-1]])
326: 
327:     # Package into a posterior

22:     r"""Standard model for HMM transitions.
23: 
24:     We place a Dirichlet prior over the rows of the transition matrix $A$,
25: 
26:     $$A_k \sim \mathrm{Dir}(\beta 1_K + \kappa e_k)$$
27: 
28:     where
29: 
30:     * $1_K$ denotes a length-$K$ vector of ones,
31:     * $e_k$ denotes the one-hot vector with a 1 in the $k$-th position,
32:     * $\beta \in \mathbb{R}_+$ is the concentration, and
33:     * $\kappa \in \mathbb{R}_+$ is the `stickiness`.
34: 
35:     """
36:     def __init__(
37:             self,
38:             num_states: int,
39:             concentration: Union[Scalar, Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]]=1.1,
40:             stickiness: Union[Scalar, Float[Array, " num_states"]]=0.0
41:     ):
42:         """
43:         Args:
44:             transition_matrix[j,k]: prob(hidden(t) = k | hidden(t-1)j)
45:         """
46:         self.num_states = num_states
47:         self.concentration = \
48:             concentration * jnp.ones((num_states, num_states)) + \
49:                 stickiness * jnp.eye(num_states)
50: 
51:     def distribution(self, params: ParamsStandardHMMTransitions, state: IntScalar, inputs=None):
52:         """Return the distribution over the next state given the current state."""
53:         return tfd.Categorical(probs=params.transition_matrix[state])

55:     def initialize(
56:             self,
57:             key: Optional[Array]=None,
58:             method="prior",
59:             transition_matrix: Optional[Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]]=None
60:     ) -> Tuple[ParamsStandardHMMTransitions, ParamsStandardHMMTransitions]:
61:         """Initialize the model parameters and their corresponding properties.
62: 
63:         Args:
64:             key (_type_, optional): _description_. Defaults to None.
65:             method (str, optional): _description_. Defaults to "prior".
66:             transition_matrix (_type_, optional): _description_. Defaults to None.
67: 
68:         Returns:
69:             _type_: _description_
70:         """
71:         if transition_matrix is None:
72:             if key is None:
73:                 raise ValueError("key must be provided if transition_matrix is not provided.")
74:             else:
75:                 transition_matrix_sample = jr.dirichlet(key, self.concentration)
76:                 transition_matrix = cast(Float[Array, "num_states num_states"], transition_matrix_sample)
77: 
78:         # Package the results into dictionaries
79:         params = ParamsStandardHMMTransitions(transition_matrix=transition_matrix)
80:         props = ParamsStandardHMMTransitions(transition_matrix=ParameterProperties(constrainer=tfb.SoftmaxCentered()))
81:         return params, props

83:     def log_prior(self, params: ParamsStandardHMMTransitions) -> Scalar:
84:         """Compute the log prior probability of the parameters."""
85:         return tfd.Dirichlet(self.concentration).log_prob(params.transition_matrix).sum()
86: 
87:     def _compute_transition_matrices(
88:             self, params: ParamsStandardHMMTransitions, inputs=None
89:     ) -> Float[Array, "num_states num_states"]:
90:         """Compute the transition matrices."""
91:         return params.transition_matrix

94:             self,
95:             params,
96:             posterior: HMMPosterior,
97:             inputs=None
98:     ) -> Union[Float[Array, "num_states num_states"],
99:                Float[Array, "num_timesteps_minus_1 num_states num_states"]]:
100:         """Collect the sufficient statistics for the model."""
101:         return posterior.trans_probs

103:     def initialize_m_step_state(self, params, props):
104:         """Initialize the state for the M-step."""
105:         return None

107:     def m_step(
108:             self,
109:             params: ParamsStandardHMMTransitions,
110:             props: ParamsStandardHMMTransitions,
111:             batch_stats: Float[Array, "batch num_states num_states"],
112:             m_step_state: Any
113:         ) -> Tuple[ParamsStandardHMMTransitions, Any]:
114:         """Perform the M-step of the EM algorithm."""
115:         if props.transition_matrix.trainable:
116:             if self.num_states == 1:
117:                 transition_matrix = jnp.array([[1.0]])
118:             else:
119:                 expected_trans_counts = batch_stats.sum(axis=0)
120:                 transition_matrix = tfd.Dirichlet(self.concentration + expected_trans_counts).mode()
121:             params = params._replace(transition_matrix=transition_matrix)

177:     # All SSMs support sampling
178:     def sample(
179:         self,
180:         params: ParameterSet,
181:         key: PRNGKeyT,
182:         num_timesteps: int,
183:         inputs: Optional[Float[Array, "num_timesteps input_dim"]]=None
184:     ) -> Tuple[Float[Array, "num_timesteps state_dim"],
185:               Float[Array, "num_timesteps emission_dim"]]:
186:         r"""Sample states $z_{1:T}$ and emissions $y_{1:T}$ given parameters $\theta$ and (optionally) inputs $u_{1:T}$.
187: 
188:         Args:
189:             params: model parameters $\theta$
190:             key: random number generator
191:             num_timesteps: number of timesteps $T$
192:             inputs: inputs $u_{1:T}$
193: 
194:         Returns:
195:             latent states and emissions
196: 
197:         """
198:         def _step(prev_state, args):
199:             """Sample the next state and emission given the previous state and input."""
200:             key, inpt = args
201:             key1, key2 = jr.split(key, 2)
202:             state = self.transition_distribution(params, prev_state, inpt).sample(seed=key2)
203:             emission = self.emission_distribution(params, state, inpt).sample(seed=key1)
204:             return state, (state, emission)
205: 
206:         # Sample the initial state
207:         key1, key2, key = jr.split(key, 3)
208:         initial_input = tree_map(lambda x: x[0], inputs)
209:         initial_state = self.initial_distribution(params, initial_input).sample(seed=key1)
210:         initial_emission = self.emission_distribution(params, initial_state, initial_input).sample(seed=key2)
211: 
212:         # Sample the remaining emissions and states
213:         next_keys = jr.split(key, num_timesteps - 1)
214:         next_inputs = tree_map(lambda x: x[1:], inputs)
215:         _, (next_states, next_emissions) = lax.scan(_step, initial_state, (next_keys, next_inputs))
216: 
217:         # Concatenate the initial state and emission with the following ones
218:         expand_and_cat = lambda x0, x1T: jnp.concatenate((jnp.expand_dims(x0, 0), x1T))
219:         states = tree_map(expand_and_cat, initial_state, next_states)
220:         emissions = tree_map(expand_and_cat, initial_emission, next_emissions)
221:         return states, emissions

357:     def fit_em(
358:         self,
359:         params: ParameterSet,
360:         props: PropertySet,
361:         emissions: Union[Real[Array, "num_timesteps emission_dim"],
362:                          Real[Array, "num_batches num_timesteps emission_dim"]],
363:         inputs: Optional[Union[Float[Array, "num_timesteps input_dim"],
364:                                Float[Array, "num_batches num_timesteps input_dim"]]]=None,
365:         num_iters: int=50,
366:         verbose: bool=True,
367:         print_every: int=1,
368:     ) -> Tuple[ParameterSet, Float[Array, " num_iters"]]:
369:         r"""Compute parameter MLE/ MAP estimate using Expectation-Maximization (EM).
370: 
371:         EM aims to find parameters that maximize the marginal log probability,
372: 
373:         $$\theta^\star = \mathrm{argmax}_\theta \; \log p(y_{1:T}, \theta \mid u_{1:T})$$
374: 
375:         It does so by iteratively forming a lower bound (the "E-step") and then maximizing it (the "M-step").
376: 
377:         *Note:* ``emissions`` *and* ``inputs`` *can either be single sequences or batches of sequences.*
378: 
379:         Args:
380:             params: model parameters $\theta$. Parameters you supply yourself must have the
381:                 same shapes and dtypes that ``initialize`` produces.
382:             props: properties specifying which parameters should be learned
383:             emissions: one or more sequences of emissions
384:             inputs: one or more sequences of corresponding inputs
385:             num_iters: number of iterations of EM to run
386:             verbose: whether or not to show a progress bar. Use ``False`` when calling
387:                 ``fit_em`` inside ``jit`` or ``vmap``.
388:             print_every: number of EM iterations between progress bar updates. Ignored when
389:                 ``verbose=False``.
390: 
391:         Returns:
392:             tuple of new parameters and log likelihoods over the course of EM iterations.
393: 
394:         """
395: 
396:         # Make sure the emissions and inputs have batch dimensions
397:         batch_emissions = ensure_array_has_batch_dim(emissions, self.emission_shape)
398:         batch_inputs = ensure_array_has_batch_dim(inputs, self.inputs_shape)
399: 
400:         def em_step(carry, _):
401:             """Perform one EM step."""
402:             params, m_step_state = carry
403:             batch_stats, lls = vmap(partial(self.e_step, params))(batch_emissions, batch_inputs)
404:             lp = self.log_prior(params) + lls.sum()
405:             params, m_step_state = self.m_step(params, props, batch_stats, m_step_state)
406:             return (params, m_step_state), lp
407: 
408:         @partial(jit, static_argnums=1)
409:         def run_em(carry, num_steps):
410:             """Run `num_steps` EM steps."""
411:             return lax.scan(em_step, carry, xs=None, length=num_steps)
412: 
413:         if num_iters <= 0:
414:             return params, jnp.array([])
415: 
416:         # The scan carries (params, m_step_state), so their structure, shapes and dtypes must
417:         # not change between iterations; initialize() produces parameters that match the M-step.
418:         carry = (params, self.initialize_m_step_state(params, props))
419:         if not verbose:
420:             (params, _), log_probs = run_em(carry, num_iters)
421:             return params, log_probs
422: 
423:         if not isinstance(print_every, Integral) or print_every < 1:
424:             raise ValueError(f"print_every must be a positive integer, got {print_every!r}")
425: 
426:         # Run `print_every` iterations per dispatch and update the bar in between. The bar counts
427:         # dispatched blocks without waiting for the device, so it can run ahead of the computation.
428:         log_probs = []
429:         pbar = progress_bar(range(num_iters))
430:         pbar.update(0)
431:         for start in range(0, num_iters, print_every):
432:             num_steps = min(print_every, num_iters - start)
433:             carry, chunk_log_probs = run_em(carry, num_steps)
434:             log_probs.append(chunk_log_probs)
435:             pbar.update(start + num_steps)
436:         return carry[0], jnp.concatenate(log_probs)

13: def big_log_joint(initial_probs, transition_matrix, log_likelihoods):
14:     """Compute the big log joint probability array
15: 
16:     Args:
17:         initial_probs (_type_): _description_
18:         transition_matrix (_type_): _description_
19:         log_lkhds (_type_): _description_
20:     """
21:     num_timesteps, num_states = log_likelihoods.shape
22:     flat_log_joint = jnp.zeros(num_states**num_timesteps)
23: 
24:     # Compute each entry in the exponentially large log joint table
25:     for states in it.product(*([jnp.arange(num_states)] * num_timesteps)):
26:         states = jnp.array(states)
27:         lp = jnp.log(initial_probs[states[0]])
28:         lp += jnp.log(transition_matrix)[states[:-1], states[1:]].sum()
29:         lp += log_likelihoods[jnp.arange(num_timesteps), states].sum()
30:         flat_index = jnp.ravel_multi_index(states, (num_states,) * num_timesteps)
31:         flat_log_joint = flat_log_joint.at[flat_index].set(lp)
32: 
33:     return flat_log_joint.reshape((num_states,) * num_timesteps)

36: def random_hmm_args(key, num_timesteps, num_states, scale=1.0):
37:     """
38:     Generate random arguments for the HMM functions.
39:     """
40:     k1, k2, k3 = jr.split(key, 3)
41:     initial_probs = jr.uniform(k1, (num_states,))
42:     initial_probs /= initial_probs.sum()
43:     transition_matrix = jr.uniform(k2, (num_states, num_states))
44:     transition_matrix /= transition_matrix.sum(1, keepdims=True)
45:     log_likelihoods = scale * jr.normal(k3, (num_timesteps, num_states))
46:     return initial_probs, transition_matrix, log_likelihoods

48: def random_hmm_args_nonstationary(key, num_timesteps, num_states, scale=1.0):
49:     """
50:     Generate random *time-varying* arguments for the HMM functions.
51:     """
52:     k1, k2, k3 = jr.split(key, 3)
53:     initial_probs = jr.uniform(k1, (num_states,))
54:     initial_probs /= initial_probs.sum()
55:     log_likelihoods = scale * jr.normal(k3, (num_timesteps, num_states))
56: 
57:     # we use numpy so we can assign to the matrix.
58:     # Then we convert to jnp.
59:     keys_A = jr.split(k2, num_timesteps - 1)
60:     trans_mat = jnp.zeros((num_timesteps - 1, num_states, num_states))
61:     for t in range(num_timesteps - 1):
62:         A = jr.uniform(keys_A[t], (num_states, num_states))
63:         A /= A.sum(1, keepdims=True)
64:         trans_mat = trans_mat.at[t].set(A)
65: 
66:     return initial_probs, trans_mat, log_likelihoods

106: def ensure_array_has_batch_dim(tree, instance_shapes):
107:     """Add a batch dimension to a PyTree, if necessary.
108: 
109:     Example: If `tree` is an array of shape (T, D) where `T` is
110:     the number of time steps and `D` is the emission dimension,
111:     and if `instance_shapes` is a tuple (D,), then the return
112:     value is the array with an added batch dimension, with
113:     shape (1, T, D).
114: 
115:     Example: If `tree` is an array of shape (N,TD) and
116:     `instance_shapes` is a tuple (D,), then the return
117:     value is simply `tree`, since it already has a batch
118:     dimension (of length N).
119: 
120:     Example: If `tree = (A, B)` is a tuple of arrays with
121:     `A.shape = (100,2)` `B.shape = (100,4)`, and
122:     `instances_shapes = ((2,), (4,))`, then the return value
123:     is equivalent to `(jnp.expand_dims(A, 0), jnp.expand_dims(B, 0))`.
124: 
125:     Args:
126:         tree (_type_): PyTree whose leaves' shapes are either
127:             (batch, length) + instance_shape or (length,) + instance_shape.
128:             If the latter, this function adds a batch dimension of 1 to
129:             each leaf node.
130: 
131:         instance_shape (_type_): matching PyTree where the "leaves" are
132:             tuples of integers specifying the shape of one "instance" or
133:             entry in the array.
134:     """
135:     def _expand_dim(x, shp):
136:         """Add a batch dimension to an array, if necessary."""
137:         ndim = len(shp)
138:         assert x.ndim > ndim, "array does not match expected shape!"
139:         assert all([(d1 == d2) for d1, d2 in zip(x.shape[-ndim:], shp)]), \
140:             "array does not match expected shape!"
141: 
142:         if x.ndim == ndim + 2:
143:             # x already has a batch dim
144:             return x
145:         elif x.ndim == ndim + 1:
146:             # x has a leading time dimension but no batch dim
147:             return jnp.expand_dims(x, 0)
148:         else:
149:             raise Exception("array has too many dimensions!")
150: 
151:     if tree is None:
152:         return None
153:     else:
154:         return tree_map(_expand_dim, tree, instance_shapes)

60: def trainable_flags(props: PropertySet) -> List[bool]:
61:     """List the ``trainable`` flag of every :class:`ParameterProperties` in ``props``.
62: 
63:     Args:
64:         props: (nested) named tuple whose leaf values are ParameterProperties.
65: 
66:     Returns:
67:         flags: list of boolean ``trainable`` flags, one per property.
68:     """
69:     is_leaf = lambda node: isinstance(node, (ParameterProperties,))
70:     return [prop.trainable for prop in tree_leaves(props, is_leaf=is_leaf)]
71:

73: def ensure_all_or_none_trainable(props: PropertySet, what: str = "emission parameters") -> bool:
74:     """Raise if some but not all of the properties in ``props`` are frozen.
75: 
76:     Args:
77:         props: (nested) named tuple whose leaf values are ParameterProperties.
78:         what: name for the parameters in ``props``.
79: 
80:     Returns:
81:         all_trainable: True if all properties are trainable, False if all are frozen.
82:     """
83:     flags = trainable_flags(props)
84:     if any(flags) and not all(flags):
85:         raise NotImplementedError(
86:             f"This model's fit_em() does not support fitting some but not all of the "
87:             f"{what}; set them all trainable or all frozen, or use fit_sgd().")
88:     return all(flags)

91: def to_unconstrained(params: ParameterSet, props: PropertySet) -> ParameterSet:
92:     """Convert the constrained parameters to unconstrained form.
93: 
94:     Args:
95:         params: (nested) named tuple whose leaf values are DeviceArrays containing
96:                               parameter values.
97:         props: matching named tuple whose leaf values are ParameterProperties,
98:                 containing an optional bijector that converts to unconstrained form,
99:                 and a boolean flag specifying if the parameter is trainable or not.
100: 
101:     Returns:
102:         unc_params: named tuple containing parameters in unconstrained form.
103: 
104:     """
105:     to_unc = lambda value, prop: prop.constrainer.inverse(value) \
106:         if prop.constrainer is not None else value
107:     is_leaf = lambda node: isinstance(node, (ParameterProperties,))
108:     return tree_map(to_unc, params, props, is_leaf=is_leaf)
109:

111: def from_unconstrained(unc_params: ParameterSet, props: PropertySet) -> ParameterSet:
112:     """Convert the unconstrained parameters to constrained form.
113: 
114:     Args:
115:         unc_params: (nested) named tuple whose leaf values are DeviceArrays containing
116:                               unconstrained parameter values.
117:         props: matching named tuple whose leaf values are ParameterProperties,
118:                 containing an optional bijector that converts to unconstrained form,
119:                 and a boolean flag specifying if the parameter is trainable or not.
120: 
121:     Returns:
122:         params: named tuple containing parameters in constrained form.
123:                  If a parameter is marked with trainable=False (frozen) in the properties structure,
124:                  it will be tagged with a "stop gradient". Thus the gradient of any loss function computed
125:                  using these frozen constrained parameters will be zero.
126: 
127:     """
128:     def from_unc(unc_value, prop):
129:         """Convert the unconstrained value to constrained form."""
130:         value = prop.constrainer(unc_value) if prop.constrainer is not None else unc_value
131:         value = lax.stop_gradient(value) if not prop.trainable else value
132:         return value
